scenes.say: What costs a driver five seconds, and what costs a whole race? Here's the Formula One penalty ladder.
The mildest: plus five or ten seconds. At the pit stop the car sits still and the crew waits.
Next up, the drive-through: in, down the pit lane at the speed limit, and back out.
Harsher still, the stop-go: ten seconds in the box, and nobody touches the car.
A grid penalty: five or ten places back at the start, most often for extra engine parts.
Disqualification wipes a driver from the results, most often for a technical breach.
Then there are super licence penalty points. Twelve in twelve months, and you sit out a race.
Magnussen was the first to be banned this way, in twenty twenty-four. His twelfth point came at Monza.
This season points are rare: only for dangerous or reckless driving, or deliberate collisions.
Watch the races live on the LapRadar map.

title: F1 penalties explained: from five seconds to a race ban
